Russia launches massive overnight barrage on Ukraine, leaving nine dead Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 11/08/2026 - 13:52 GMT+2 Russia killed at least nine people in Ukraine overnight on Tuesday, as missile and drone strikes hit Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk, according to regional authorities. … More In Kyiv, the State Emergency Service said a warehouse caught fire after a ballistic missile attack and one person was wounded. Footage released by the service showed firefighters tackling flames at the scene. The capital came under attack shortly after midnight, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko reporting a ballistic missile strike. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The heaviest casualties were reported in Zaporizhzhia, where six people were killed and 19 wounded in what regional governor Ivan Fedorov described as a massive attack involving missiles and guided bombs. In Dnipropetrovsk, Russian drone and artillery strikes across five districts killed three people and wounded five, according to regional authorities. Russia's Defence Ministry said it had targeted military-industrial and transport facilities in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia. The attacks came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had received new ballistic missiles from North Korea. Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-range strikes in recent weeks, with Ukraine also targeting sites deep inside Russian territory. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/08/form.text: The wife of Sri Lanka's powerful former President Mahinda Rajapaksa was detained on Wednesday on allegations of misusing donations received for her charity when she was first lady.Police questioned Shiranthi Rajapaksa at her home and later took her before a court, which ordered her detention for a week pending investigations. Police then escorted Rajapaksa, who had one eye bandaged from recent surgery, to a vehicle to be taken to a jail.Rajapaksa was accused of misusing funds that her charity received as a donation from a state bank earmarked for the purchase of a scanner for a government hospital.The then-head of the bank also was arrested for allegedly circumventing procedures in releasing the money to the charity. The court later released him on bail.The former first couple's son, lawmaker Namal Rajapaksa, has also been detained on charges of bribery.Ex-President Rajapaksa and his family were adored by the country's majority ethnic Sinhala Buddhists after he and his brother Gotabhaya Rajapaksa led a military campaign to defeat the now-defunct Tamil Tiger rebels and end a 26-year civil war in the island nation in 2009.His popularity declined after his re-election in 2010 however, over rampant allegations of bribery, corruption and the stifling of freedoms, leading to his defeat while seeking a third term in 2015.His family had wielded unbridled power — with his son, brothers, nephews and nieces holding top government positions.The family made a comeback in 2019 when security emerged as a key concern following Islamic State-inspired suicide bomb attacks that killed 267 people in churches and hotels on Easter Sunday.Gotabhaya Rajapaksa was elected president later that year, but then the country suffered an economic crash brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic, a tourism downturn and his economic decisions.He was forced to resign and flee the country amid massive public protests.Anura Kumara Dissanayake later replaced him and became president, for which he campaigned on an anti-corruption ticket in 2024, promising to take action against anyone suspected of corruption in the Rajapaksa family and administrations that preceded them.
